body.title: llama cpp server with quantized 3B llm model to generate xlsforms
body.body: ## Description Added an LLM-based form builder to the `/builder` route. Users describe a survey in plain language (e.g., `"I want to survey water points in rural areas"`) and the system generates a valid, downloadable `XLSForm` compatible with `ODK`. ## Key Features Natural language → structured XLSForm generation Integrated preview of generated forms before download Downloadable .xlsx using existing export utilities Designed to produce forms compatible with ODK Central **Architecture** ``` Browser → FormBuilder.vue → /api/generate → Go backend → llama.cpp (Qwen2.5-3B) → JSON response ↓ FormPreview.vue ← XLSFormDocument ↓ Download .xlsx via existing export utils ``` ## Implementation Details - Added `/api/generate` endpoint in Go backend to interface with the `LLM` - Integrated local `LLM` inference using `llama.cpp` with `Qwen2.5-3B` - Implemented prompt engineering in prompts.go to ensure a valid `XLSForm` structure - Updated chat UI to display a live preview of generated forms - Modified chat UI to give a preview of the generated XLSForm ## Deployment Notes The LLM model is not included in the repository due to size constraints For deployment: - Option 1: Host the model on the server and mount it into the container - Option 2: Use an external hosting solution such as Hugging Face and connect via API endpoint ## Future Improvements - Improve prompt templates for different survey domains - Add validation layer for stricter XLSForm compliance - Support custom question types and reusable templates - Enable streaming responses for better UX

body.title: Tree utilities + XLSForm export pipeline
body.body:
**Summary**

  - Add TypeScript data model for XLSForm documents
  - Add tree manipulation utilities for the survey node tree
  - Add xlsx export pipeline that serializes an XLSFormDocument into a valid .xlsx file via SheetJS with survey, choices, and settings sheets
  - Add e2e verification script that round-trips a bilingual form through pyxform-http
  - Add vitest, test infrastructure, and unit tests
  
  **Testing**
  
Start pyxform-http: `docker run --rm -d -p 8086:80 --name pyxform-e2e ghcr.io/getodk/pyxform-http:latest`
  - Run `npx tsx scripts/verify-e2e.ts`
  - Verify tests pass
  - To clean up `docker rm -f pyxform-e2e`

  **Manual test**

  - Generate the file `npx tsx scripts/verify-e2e.ts --save-only`
  - Upload field_survey_v1.xlsx to [https://getodk.org/xlsform/](https://getodk.org/xlsform/)
  - Clean up `rm field_survey_v1.xlsx`

If you are feeling fancy upload it through our upload page and preview it from the examples page.

Closes #23

body.title: For container-based frontends, use runtime env injection instead of baked build vars
body.body:
- Having to rebuild a container for every change in environment / env vars on the frontend isn't ideal.
- It's fine running `pnpm dev` locally with a dotenv, but for containers we need a nicer approach.
- Added an entrypoint and other config to allow specifying the env vars at runtime.
- Will add a tiny startup delay, cached by nginx on second load, so not a big deal.
- Allows for easier testing / swapping of env vars - in particular we can specify the API URL as a helm chart variable.

body.title: Add form preview button using ODK WebForms (to see rendered ODK form)
body.body:
Adds XLSForm preview functionality by converting forms to XForm XML and opening them in the ODK Web Forms preview site.

Chose the alternative approach of using the existing ODK Web Forms preview site rather than embedding the webforms library directly. This ensures we always use the latest ODK code without maintenance overhead.

- **Preview Button**: Added to each form card with loading state during conversion
- **Backend Conversion API** : Downloads XLSForm, converts to XForm XML via pyxform-http, uploads to AWS S3
- **Dual S3 Architecture**: Local MinIO for development uploads, production AWS S3 for converted XML

**Notes:** 

ODK Web Forms preview requires XForm XML format, not XLSForm. Additionally, CSP restrictions prevent loading forms from localhost URLs.

**Implemented solution:**
1. Converts XLSForm to XForm using self hosted pyxform-http
2. Uploads converted XML to production S3
3. Passes S3 URL to ODK Web Forms preview site

Closes #15

body.title: Add XLSForm Upload Feature with S3 Integration
body.body:
This PR implements a complete file upload system that lets users submit XLSForms with metadata to S3.

## Key Changes

### Backend Service

- Go microservice for generating S3 pre-signed URLs
- Supports both AWS S3 (prod) and MinIO (local)
- CORS enabled REST API with `/api/presigned-url` and `/api/presigned-download-url` endpoints
- Health check endpoint for monitoring

### Frontend Features

- Upload page with intuitive form for XLSForm submission
- File dropzone using HOTOSM UI component
- Form fields: title, location, description, tags, external link
- Real time validation 
- Success dialog with navigation to examples
- Mobile responsive

### Upload Flow

1. User fills form and selects XLSForm file
2. Frontend requests pre-signed URL from backend
3. File uploads directly to S3/Min IO using pre-signed URL
4. Frontend fetches current metadata.json from S3/MinIO
5. New form entry appended to metadata
6. Updated metadata uploaded back to S3/MinIO
7. Success confirmation shown

### Local Development

- MinIO integration for S3 compatible local storage
- Docker Compose setup for backend and MinIO services
- No AWS account required for testing

## Testing

### Quick Start

1. Start backend services with Docker:
```
docker compose up
```

2. This launches:
   - Backend API at http://localhost:3000
   - MinIO (local S3) at http://localhost:9000
   - MinIO Console at http://localhost:9001

3. Verify backend is ready:
```
docker compose ps

curl http://localhost:3000/health
```

4. Start frontend locally:
```
pnpm install
pnpm run dev
```


5. Test the upload flow:
   - Fill out the form
   - Drag and drop an .xlsx file or click to browse
   - Click "Upload Form"
   - Wait for success dialog

6. Verify the upload:
   - Click "View Examples" in success dialog
   - Confirm your test form appears in the list
   - Click "Download Form" to verify file uploaded correctly
   - Note: "Open Form" shows alert in local mode 

7. Check MinIO storage:
   - Open http://localhost:9001
   - Login: minioadmin / minioadmin
   - Navigate to xlsforms bucket
   - Confirm both .xlsx file and metadata.json exist

9. Cleanup when done:
```
docker compose down
```

### What to Test

- Form validation 
- File upload with various .xlsx files
- Multiple form submissions 
- Empty state when no forms exist
- Responsive layout on different screen sizes
- Cache busting. Upload form, verify it appears immediately
- Success dialog and navigation flow

Closes #4 and #3

body.title: Integrate Web Awesome components and HOT UI design system
body.body: This PR establishes the foundation for the XLSForm builder by integrating Web Awesome components and HOT UI design system. The main focus was creating a nice looking, intuitive, mobile optimized layout while maintaining consistency with HOT's visual identity. ### Design System Foundation - Set up SCSS with HOT design system variables and mixins - Imported font families to match HOT typography standards - Created reusable card mixin for consistent component styling ### Component Integration - Integrated Web Awesome card components - Implemented responsive CSS grid layout (1/2/3 columns based on screen size) - Added proper button styling with flex-wrap for mobile optimization - Ensured equal width card behavior across all screen sizes ### Development Tooling - Added Prettier with single quotes and import sorting - Configured ESLint for Vue 3 + TypeScript following HOT standards - Set up Sass compilation for design system integration **_Note: I went ahead and included Prettier/ESLint setup as part of this effort to ensure code quality, but happy to remove if not desired. I tried to match the linting rules observed in other HOT repositories._** ### Screenshots ### Known Issues **HOT Components**: I ran into some issues with the HOT components from [@hotosm/ui](https://github.com/hotosm/ui): - Mobile styling doesn't respond properly on smaller screens - Unable to override certain fonts to match the typography used throughout the app I attempted to target and override these styles without any success. I believe these issues would be best addressed directly in the `@hotosm/ui` repository itself rather than trying to work around them here. ### Testing Notes - Responsive design works on mobile, tablet, and desktop - Cards maintain equal width across different content lengths - Components render properly with Web Awesome styling - Layout and components align with HOT design standards

body.body:
## Summary
Resolves pnpm lockfile inconsistencies that were causing build failures in CI environments with frozen lockfile settings.

  ## Changes
  - **Updated pnpm-lock.yaml** to match current package.json specifications
  - **Resolved version mismatches** for core dependencies:
    - `@awesome.me/webawesome`: 3.0.0-beta.3 → 3.0.0-beta.5
    - `@hotosm/ui`: 0.3.2-b9 → 0.3.4b2
  - **Added missing dev dependencies** that were present in package.json but missing from lockfile:
    - ESLint configuration and plugins
    - Prettier and TypeScript tooling
    - Sass and build tools

  ## Technical Details
  - Ran `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` to resolve dependency conflicts
  - Verified all packages are properly aligned between manifest and lockfile
